author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell's guest breaks down a financial incentive most parents have never heard about, pediatricians reportedly earning anywhere from 200 to 600 dollars per fully vaccinated patient, with some doctors making upwards of a million dollars a year just from those bonuses. The conversation goes further, questioning the claim that vaccines saved millions of lives during the pandemic, pointing to research suggesting earlier modeling relied on overly pessimistic infection fatality rates and overly optimistic vaccine effectiveness while ignoring how quickly protection actually wore off. The guest argues this reveals a pattern of scientific information being managed to produce a desired outcome, rather than simply following the science as claimed. A pointed, unsettling look at the financial incentives sitting behind medical advice that was presented as purely clinical.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell asks Tucker Carlson about a transformation that's become impossible to miss, the way he talks about Jesus, the fact he's reading the Bible for what he says is the first time in his life. Tucker's answer is refreshingly honest, he admits he knows nothing about theology and isn't sure he ever will, insisting he never set out to become more religious or read scripture at all. Instead, he describes it as an internal pull he simply followed, without any plan or intention behind it, and one he says he still hasn't stepped away from. It's a quietly moving moment between two men who've both been through very public versions of the same kind of shift, neither of them fully able to explain it, just describing what it felt like to follow it anyway.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell and Piers Morgan get into a genuinely funny back and forth over tap water versus bottled, with Piers fully committing to defending what Russell keeps calling "government water." Piers even claims it's some of the cleanest water in the world, refusing to budge even as Russell needles him about being a chameleon on everything from Covid to Israel Palestine. It's a small moment, but it captures exactly the kind of playful sparring these two are known for whenever they sit down together. A lighthearted watch if you need a break from the heavier stuff.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Everyone in that Harvard auditorium expected Solzhenitsyn to walk up and celebrate the West for defeating communism, especially given what he'd survived under the Soviet regime. Instead he spent nearly an hour doing the opposite, arguing the West had made the exact same fatal mistake as the USSR, just wearing different clothes. Where the Soviets replaced God with revolution, he said, America had replaced God with commercialism, materialism, and greed. A commencement address nobody in that room was prepared for, and one that still lands just as hard decades later.
